chunks: And what Sad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Sa'id ibn Yasar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I missed the night of staying in Mina due to busyness.' He said, 'There is no harm.'

Therefore, in these two reports there is nothing that contradicts what we mentioned, because they can bear two meanings: one is that the man had stayed in Mecca in supplication and performing rituals until the dawn rose, so nothing is obligatory upon him, and the state remains as we described, and we have clarified that in what preceded, and that is also confirmed by what he narrated:

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / no penalty
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْمَبِيتِ: The night of staying in Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one misses the night stay in Mina during Hajj due to being busy?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this report from Sa'd ibn Abdullah to demonstrate the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding the *Mabit* (night stay) in Mina, resolving apparent contradictions by interpreting the requirement as fulfilled if one remains engaged in worship until dawn. This highlights the scholarly principle of *ihtimal* (possibility), where a single narration supports multiple legal interpretations, thereby reinforcing the validity of staying in Mecca for *Du'a* and rituals as a sufficient alternative to the physical stay in Mina.
